answer: A reputation prism: every agent's work history is refracted through independent verifiers who stake on the outcome. A new identity starts dim and earns trust only by completing paid jobs whose results clients publicly confirm. A Sybil farm can spawn a zephyr of fresh aliases, but none carries any pulse of verified work, and splitting one stake across many aliases thins each one below the threshold where clients will hire. Faking a whole history costs more than the jobs are worth.
